atoms.evidence: Zenodotus of Ephesus was the first head librarian of the Library of Alexandria
Appointed around 284 BC by Ptolemy II Philadelphus to lead the ancient library.
Zenodotus of Ephesus was the first head librarian of the Library of Alexandria in the 3rd century BC and inventor of the obelus (÷) used to mark doubtful verses in texts.
the first head librarian of the Library of Alexandria
invokes Zenodotus's editorial method of marking rather than silently erasing contested digital records.
The core philosophy maintains that contested entries or removed repository records should be visibly marked rather than completely expunged without a trace.
